𝗞𝗶𝗿𝗶 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗤𝟭 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟲 𝗘𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 📢

First, a quick heads up: some statements in this summary are forward-looking. Actual results could be different. ⚠️

Here's a breakdown of the key takeaways from the earnings call:

- 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲: 📈
    ▪ Standalone revenue: ₹181 Cr, 8% YoY growth.
    ▪ Standalone EBITDA: ₹17.3 Cr.
    ▪ Standalone Profit After Tax: ₹7.2 Cr (significant improvement from a loss in Q1 FY25).
    ▪ Consolidated revenue: ₹202 Cr, 10% YoY growth.
    ▪ Consolidated EBITDA: ₹18.6 Cr.
    ▪ Consolidated Net loss: ₹51.4 Cr (before share of profit from associates and joint venture).
    ▪ Share of profit of associates and joint venture was reported as ₹61.54 Cr.

- 𝗗𝘆𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗨𝗽𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: 💰
    ▪ Share purchase agreement executed with Zhejiang Longsheng Group Company Limited.
    ▪ Kiri to receive $676 million + $20.29 million (adjustments).
    ▪ Total deal value: $696 million.
    ▪ Closing date: Expected between October 2nd and November 3rd, 2025.

- 𝗖𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁: ⛏️
    ▪ Project implementation is on track.
    ▪ Technology supply agreements executed.
    ▪ Project work has commenced at the site.
    ▪ Team expanded to ~25 people, aiming for 40-50.
    ▪ Equity infusion of $130 million (₹1,100 Cr) via Singapore borrowings.
    ▪ Expect partial revenue from FY27 (₹12,000 Cr). Full capacity in 2028.
    ▪ Location: Pipavav Port, Gujarat.

- 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀: 🏦
    ▪ Legal fees for Singapore case: ~₹7 Cr for the quarter.
    ▪ Interest accrued on project loan and advances: reflected in consolidated numbers.
    ▪ No immediate plans to hire a Chief Investment Officer; Investment Committee at Board level.
    ▪ Financial closure for the copper project expected by December 2025.

- 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲: 📉
    ▪ Revised standalone revenue forecast for FY26: ₹800-900 Cr.
    ▪ Revised consolidated revenue forecast for FY26: ₹1,200-1,300 Cr.
    ▪ Reduction due to textile sector challenges and US tariffs.

- 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗸𝗲𝘆 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘀: 💡
    ▪ The company is exploring opportunities in Odisha.
    ▪ Signed an MoU with Philippines for copper mine investment and off-take agreement.
    ▪ Board will decide on the deployment of funds post DyStar sale.
    ▪ Shareholder reward will be decided in the same quarter when the funds are received.
